The '''2022–23 season''' was '''[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool Football Club]]''''s [[List of Liverpool F.C. seasons|131st season]] in existence and their 61st consecutive season in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in England|English football]]. Coming off their [[2021–22 Liverpool F.C. season|2021–22 campaign]], Liverpool competed in this season's editions of the [[2022–23 Premier League|Premier League]], [[2022–23 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2022–23 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].

Liverpool kicked off the season with a 3–1 victory over reigning [[2021–22 Premier League|Premier League champions]] [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2022 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] for their 16th Community Shield and [[List of football clubs in England by competitive honours won|68th official trophy]], the latter being an English record. Furthermore, that piece of silverware completed the set for [[Jürgen Klopp]], to win all available first-tier trophies with Liverpool at least once.<ref>[https://www.90min.com/posts/every-trophy-jurgen-klopp-has-won-at-liverpool Every trophy Jurgen Klopp has won with Liverpool]</ref>

After narrowly missing out on a possible quadruple the previous season, the 2022–23 campaign was a bitter disappointment for Liverpool. Inconsistent form in the Premier League ruled them out of the title race, whilst the Reds were knocked out of both cups in the fourth round. Liverpool's Champions League campaign also ended in disappointment as they lost 6–2 on aggregate to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League#Round of 16|round of 16]]. Despite a 11-game unbeaten run in the league at the end of the season – including 7 straight victories – this was not enough to secure a top-four position and Liverpool ultimately finished 5th, failing to qualify for [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|the next season's Champions League]] for the first time in seven years. Overall, the team's form was poor all season, which spurred major changes in the squad for the following campaign. As such, this season is widely considered as Liverpool's worst season under Klopp, with observers noting that some players' "legs had gone", particularly in midfield.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Henry |date=2024-05-10 |title=Ranking every season under Klopp - from best to worst! |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2024/05/ranking-every-season-under-jurgen-klopp-from-best-to-worst/ |access-date=2024-11-14 |website=This Is Anfield |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-14 |title=Ranking all 9 Liverpool seasons under Jurgen Klopp |url=https://onefootball.com/es/noticias/ranking-all-9-liverpool-seasons-under-jurgen-klopp-38942492 |access-date=2024-11-14 |website=OneFootball |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ritchie |first=Calum |date=2024-01-26 |title=We have ranked each of Jurgen Klopp's 9 seasons at Liverpool |url=https://www.givemesport.com/ranking-all-9-liverpool-seasons-under-jurgen-klopp/ |access-date=2024-11-14 |website=GiveMeSport |language=en}}</ref> 

This season was the first since [[2015–16 Liverpool F.C. season|2015–16]] without [[Sadio Mané]], who transferred to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] and the first since [[2014–15 Liverpool F.C. season|2014–15]] without [[Divock Origi]], who departed to [[AC Milan]]. At the end of the season, it was announced that [[Roberto Firmino]], [[James Milner]], [[Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain]] and [[Naby Keïta]] were confirmed to leave the club as their contracts would not be renewed.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://offsidetrap.in/chance-of-top-four-for-liverpool/ | title=Chance of Top Four for Liverpool: Champions League Spot up for Grab: Liverpool vs Aston Villa | date=20 May 2023 }}</ref>

==Season overview==
On 30 July 2022, Liverpool opened the 2022–23 season by achieving victory in the [[2022 FA Community Shield]] with a 3–1 win over Manchester City.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/61587053 |title=Liverpool 3 Man City 1: Live |website=BBC Sport |date=30 July 2022 |access-date=10 August 2022}}</ref> On 27 August 2022, Liverpool achieved a [[Liverpool F.C. 9–0 AFC Bournemouth|9–0]] win over [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] in the [[2022–23 Premier League|Premier League]] in which [[Roberto Firmino]] scored his 100th goal for Liverpool.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3543857/2022/08/29/roberto-firmino-100-liverpool-goals/ |title=Analysing Roberto Firmino's 100 Liverpool goals |date=29 August 2022 |website=The Athletic |access-date=29 August 2022}}</ref> The match was the [[List of highest-scoring Premier League matches#Biggest winning margin|joint-largest win in the history of the Premier League]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hafez |first1=Shamoon |title=Liverpool 9-0 Bournemouth: Diaz, Elliott, Alexander-Arnold, Firmino, Van Dijk all score |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62614438 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=28 August 2022 |date=27 August 2022}}</ref> and equalled Liverpool's biggest ever win in the top flight, achieving [[Liverpool 9–0 Crystal Palace (1989)|the same scoreline]] at [[Anfield]] in the [[1989–90 Football League First Division|1989–90 season]] against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. The match was also Bournemouth's worst ever top-flight defeat. On 12 October 2022, Liverpool achieved a 7–1 away victory over [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. In the game, [[Mohamed Salah]] broke [[Bafétimbi Gomis]]'s record for the fastest [[List of UEFA Champions League hat-tricks|Champions League hat-trick]] of all time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rangers 1-7 Liverpool|work= BBC Sport |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63186550 |access-date=31 August 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=12 October 2022 |title=Salah breaks Champions League record with fastest hat trick |newspaper=The Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/soccer/salah-breaks-champions-league-record-with-fastest-hat-trick/2022/10/12/bb9bd0c0-4a74-11ed-8153-96ee97b218d2_story.html |access-date=12 October 2022}}</ref> 

On 28 December 2022, [[Cody Gakpo]] agreed to sign for Liverpool for a [[transfer fee]] of between £35.4 to £44.3&nbsp;million (€40 to €50&nbsp;million) once the transfer window opened on 1 January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-reach-agreement-cody-gakpo-transfer |title=Liverpool reach agreement for Cody Gakpo transfer |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=28 December 2022 |access-date=28 December 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64104472 |title=Cody Gakpo: Liverpool reach agreement with PSV Eindhoven to sign forward |website=BBC Sport |date=28 December 2022 |access-date=28 December 2022}}</ref> On 5 March 2023, Liverpool recorded their biggest ever competitive win against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] with an historic [[Liverpool F.C. 7–0 Manchester United F.C.|7–0]] victory at Anfield. [[Cody Gakpo]], [[Darwin Núñez]], and Mohamed Salah all scored braces with [[Roberto Firmino]] netting the final goal. This surpassed Liverpool’s previous record set in October 1895, a 7–1 victory in the [[1895–96 Football League#Second Division|Second Division]]. Furthermore, this was Manchester United's [[List of Manchester United F.C. records and statistics#Record defeats|joint-biggest ever defeat]] and the heaviest since [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] beat them by the same scoreline in [[1931–32 Football League#Second Division|1931]].<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty|first=Phil |title=Liverpool 7-0 Manchester United: Reds thrash old rivals in Anfield rout|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64775037|access-date=5 March 2023|work=BBC Sport |date=5 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Liverpool thrash Manchester United 7-0 in historic defeat |url=https://news.sky.com/story/liverpool-thrash-man-united-7-0-in-historic-defeat-12826896 |first=Andy |last=Hayes |access-date=5 March 2023|date=5 March 2023|website=Sky News}}</ref> On 10 March 2023, Liverpool announced Firmino would leave Liverpool at the end of the season after he decided not to extend his contract. Klopp stated that he was a "little bit surprised" by the decision but wished Firmino good luck, saying that he would “be grateful forever” for his contribution to Liverpool.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liverpool FC — Jürgen Klopp on Roberto Firmino's decision to depart LFC |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/jurgen-klopp-roberto-firminos-decision-depart-lfc |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=www.liverpoolfc.com |date=March 2023 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title= 'I will be grateful forever' – Jürgen Klopp reflects on Roberto Firmino's LFC career |url= https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/460786-i-will-be-grateful-forever-jurgen-klopp-reflects-on-roberto-firmino-s-lfc-career |access-date=2023-06-02 |website=www.liverpoolfc.com |date= 2 June 2023 |language=en}}</ref> On 20 May 2023, Roberto Firmino scored his last Liverpool goal at Anfield in a 1–1 draw against Aston Villa.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/roberto-firmino-enjoys-dream-farewell-30031086|title=Firmino in tears as Anfield pays tribute to four departing Liverpool stars|first=Will|last=Freeman|date=20 May 2023|website=mirror}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65659669|title=Firmino's Liverpool farewell will see Reds 'rebuild'|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> Firmino also scored in his last ever game for Liverpool on 28 May 2023, being assisted by fellow Brazilian [[Fabinho (footballer, born 1993)|Fabinho]].<ref>{{Cite news|url= https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/firmino-scores-farewell-liverpool-southampton-draw-thriller-2023-05-28/ |title= Firmino scores on farewell as Liverpool and Southampton draw thriller |work=Reuters|date= 28 May 2023 }}</ref>

===Aftermath===
Liverpool narrowly missed out on [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] qualification, with winger [[Mohamed Salah]] describing himself as "totally devastated".<ref>{{Cite news |title= Mohamed Salah 'totally devastated' Liverpool miss out on Champions League football: 'absolutely no excuse' |publisher= EuroSport |url= https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/premier-league/2022-2023/mohamed-salah-totally-devastated-liverpool-miss-out-on-champions-league-football-absolutely-no-excus_sto9623012/story.shtml |access-date= 29 May 2023 }}</ref> It was suggested that reasons for their failure to qualify for the Champions League included the declining form of key members of the team [[Virgil van Dijk]] and [[Fabinho (footballer, born 1993)|Fabinho]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 April 2023 |first=Neil |last=Jones |title=Virgil van Dijk's form is seriously worrying for Liverpool - they must pray it's only a short-term blip |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/van-dijk-form-worrying-liverpool-pray-short-term-blip/blt58d768845945dde1 |publisher=Goal |access-date=6 May 2023 |archive-date=6 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230506222601/https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/van-dijk-form-worrying-liverpool-pray-short-term-blip/blt58d768845945dde1 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date= 17 April 2023 |first= Nick |last= Wright |title= Virgil van Dijk: Liverpool defender looks well below his best but is he on the decline or simply out of form? |url= https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11096/12855900/virgil-van-dijk-liverpool-defender-looks-well-below-his-best-but-is-he-on-the-decline-or-simply-out-of-form |publisher= Sky Sports |access-date= 6 May 2023 |archive-date= 6 May 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230506222601/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11096/12855900/virgil-van-dijk-liverpool-defender-looks-well-below-his-best-but-is-he-on-the-decline-or-simply-out-of-form |url-status= live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title= Out-of-gas Fabinho has become a symbol of Liverpool's decline |work= The Guardian |url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/nov/05/out-of-gas-fabinho-has-become-a-symbol-of-liverpools-decline |access-date= 31 March 2023 |archive-date= 31 March 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230331055839/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/nov/05/out-of-gas-fabinho-has-become-a-symbol-of-liverpools-decline |url-status= live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title= The end of an era at Liverpool? Henderson and Fabinho's struggles leave Klopp with big calls to make |work= Goal |url= https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/end-era-liverpool-henderson-fabinho-struggles-klopp-big-calls/blt6bca5000f2001a76 |access-date=29 July 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title= Past it now - Sergio Busquets, Jorginho, N'Golo Kante, Fabinho |work= GiveMeSport |url= https://www.givemesport.com/ranking-the-15-best-defensive-midfielders-in-the-world-ft-rice-rodri-caicedo/#past-it-now---sergio-busquets-jorginho-n-39-golo-kante-fabinho |access-date=28 July 2023 }}</ref> and the vast amount of injuries suffered by Liverpool players.<ref>{{Cite news |title= Klopp only willing to sign 'right player' for Liverpool despite Thiago injury|work= The Guardian |url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/aug/12/klopp-only-willing-to-sign-right-player-for-liverpool-despite-thiago-injury |access-date=29 August 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title= Why have Liverpool made such a slow start to the Premier League season?|work= The Guardian |url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/aug/23/liverpools-early-season-woes-have-variety-of-factors-behind-them |access-date=29 August 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title= Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk facing long spell on sidelines with hamstring injury|work= The Guardian |url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jan/04/liverpool-virgil-van-dijk-facing-long-spell-on-sidelines-with-hamstring-injury |access-date=29 August 2023 }}</ref> On 21 May 2023, addressing the reality of being in the [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] next [[2023–24 Liverpool F.C. season|season]], Klopp stated that Liverpool would "make [the Europa League] our competition".<ref>{{Cite news |title= Jurgen Klopp makes promise about Liverpool playing in next season's Europa League |work=90min |url= https://www.90min.com/posts/jurgen-klopp-promise-liverpool-next-season-europa-league |access-date=31 August 2023 }}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
Liverpool announced they would be touring South East Asia, starting with a match against [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|rivals]] [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in [[Bangkok]] on 12 July,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/pre-season-liverpool-take-manchester-united-bangkok |title=Pre-season: Liverpool to take on Manchester United in Bangkok |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=31 March 2022 |access-date=21 April 2022}}</ref> followed by a trip to Singapore to face [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on 15 July.<ref>{{cite news |title=Reds to face Crystal Palace in Singapore for second leg of pre-season |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/reds-face-crystal-palace-singapore-second-leg-pre-season |access-date=26 April 2022 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=26 April 2022}}</ref> On 16 June, the Reds announced a further two pre-season matches, against [[RB Leipzig]] and [[RC Strasbourg Alsace|Strasbourg]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Reds confirm Germany and Anfield pre-season fixtures |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/reds-confirm-germany-and-anfield-pre-season-fixtures |access-date=17 June 2022 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=17 June 2022}}</ref> and later announced another friendly against [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]] in Austria on 27 July.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/reds-add-salzburg-clash-series-pre-season-fixtures |title=Reds add Salzburg clash to series of pre-season fixtures |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=23 June 2022 |access-date=23 June 2022}}</ref>

During the mid-season break as a result of the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], Liverpool announced they would be travelling to [[Dubai]] to take part in the Dubai Super Cup friendly tournament, facing [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] and [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] on 11 and 16 December, respectively.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-play-lyon-and-ac-milan-dubai-super-cup |title=Liverpool to play Lyon and AC Milan in Dubai Super Cup |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=15 November 2022 |access-date=15 November 2022}}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2022–23 FA Cup}}

The club entered the competition in the third round and were drawn at home to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool to face Wolves in FA Cup third round |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-face-wolves-fa-cup-third-round |access-date=28 November 2022 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=28 November 2022}}</ref> They were drawn away to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] in the fourth round.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool to play Brighton & Hove Albion in FA Cup fourth round |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-play-brighton-hove-albion-fa-cup-fourth-round |access-date=17 January 2023 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=17 January 2023}}</ref>

===FA Community Shield===
{{main|2022 FA Community Shield}}
The traditional season curtain raiser was played between the previous season's league champions and FA Cup winners. As winners of the [[2021–22 FA Cup]], Liverpool faced [[2021–22 Premier League]] champions [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]. Normally played at [[Wembley Stadium]], this season it was played at [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]'s [[King Power Stadium]] to avoid clashes with the [[UEFA Women's Euro 2022]] competition.

===UEFA Champions League===
{{main|2022–23 UEFA Champions League}}
Liverpool entered the competition in the group stage.

{{main|2022–23 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group A}}

====Knockout phase====
{{main|2022–23 UEFA Champions League knockout phase}}
Liverpool advanced to the knockout phase as group runners-up.

=====Round of 16=====
The round of 16 draw took place on 7 November, and Liverpool were drawn to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], who they last met in the [[2022 UEFA Champions League Final|2022 final]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Liverpool to face Real Madrid in Champions League last 16|url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-face-real-madrid-champions-league-last-16|publisher=Liverpool F.C.|date=7 November 2022|access-date=7 November 2022}}</ref>
